cards.answer: Soraka is a support mage who heals allied champions. She helps control fights with slows, silence and a delayed root. AP is a learning focus for her healing and magic damage.
cards.counterplay: Avoid her damaging areas and account for her healing when choosing a target.

cards.answer: Soraka moves faster toward nearby allied champions at low health.
cards.counterplay: Account for her faster approach when pursuing a low-health ally of hers.

cards.answer: A star lands at the target location, dealing magic damage and slowing enemies hit. Hitting an enemy champion grants Soraka Rejuvenation: healing over time and bonus movement speed that fades. While she has Rejuvenation, Astral Infusion also grants it to the target ally.
cards.counterplay: Move out of the star's landing area to avoid its damage and slow and deny Soraka Rejuvenation from hitting you.

facts.claim: A star lands at the target location, dealing magic damage and slowing enemies hit.

citations.quote: If this hits at least one enemy champion, the star dust returns to Soraka to grant her Rejuvenation for a short time.
Rejuvenation: The target continually heals over time and gains bonus movement speed that decays over the duration.
If an enemy champion is hit by Starcall, Soraka recovers Health.

facts.claim: Hitting an enemy champion grants Soraka Rejuvenation: healing over time and bonus movement speed that fades.

citations.quote: While Soraka has Rejuvenation, Astral Infusion will also grant Rejuvenation to the target ally.

facts.claim: While she has Rejuvenation, Astral Infusion also grants it to the target ally.

cards.priority_reason: Avoiding Starcall limits both its control and Soraka's healing support.
uncertainties: The Wiki says both the initial hit and returning Rejuvenation projectile can be intercepted.
Soraka receives Rejuvenation and W health-cost reduction when the returning projectile arrives; the Wiki allows sharing Rejuvenation with allies from the champion hit.
The Wiki says a spell-shielded champion hit still grants Rejuvenation. The answer describes general behavior without guaranteeing projectile arrival.

cards.answer: Soraka heals another allied champion, normally spending some of her own health. While she has Rejuvenation, Astral Infusion costs less health and also grants Rejuvenation to the ally.
cards.counterplay: Avoid Starcall to limit Soraka's access to cheaper heals and shared Rejuvenation.

cards.priority_reason: Her targeted healing can keep an ally alive through focused damage.
uncertainties: Rejuvenation can fully remove the health cost at the listed highest rank.
The Wiki prohibits casting below 5% maximum health but allows casting above that threshold without enough health for the full cost; the cost cannot reduce Soraka below 1 health.
Allied decoys are also eligible targets according to the Wiki.

cards.answer: Soraka creates a zone that silences enemies inside. Enemy champions in the zone take magic damage when it appears and again when it erupts. Enemy champions still inside when it expires are rooted.
cards.counterplay: Leave the zone to escape its silence and avoid the eruption's damage and root.

citations.quote: Creates a zone at a location that silences all enemies inside.

facts.claim: Soraka creates a zone that silences enemies inside.

citations.quote: Active: Soraka creates a celestial zone at the target location that deals magic damage to enemy champions within upon casting.
Afterwards, the zone erupts to deal the same damage to enemy champions within and root them for a duration.

facts.claim: Enemy champions in the zone take magic damage when it appears and again when it erupts.

facts.claim: Enemy champions still inside when it expires are rooted.

cards.priority_reason: Silence can deny ability use, and remaining in the zone risks a root.
uncertainties: Riot describes the root for all enemies, while the Wiki explicitly describes enemy champions; the answer uses their shared champion scope.
The Wiki says spell shields do not block the silence; this does not establish their interaction with the damage or root.
Most cleanses do not remove the silence; the Wiki lists an exception for cleanses that also grant immunity.

cards.answer: Soraka instantly heals herself and all allied champions, regardless of distance. Low-health targets receive increased healing.
cards.counterplay: Account for Wish when committing to finish a low-health enemy, even when Soraka is far away.

cards.priority_reason: Global healing can change a fight even when Soraka is elsewhere.
uncertainties: The Wiki reports an immediate-respawn bug affecting ability-haste cooldown reduction and AP healing scaling; current-client behavior is not verified.
The Wiki says untargetability does not prevent the heal and describes healing across Mordekaiser's realms.
